characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/Max-2200, Cu target, operated at 40 kV and 40 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 6Cr strip is composed of austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) with austenite as major matrix phase; the δ(110) reflection (2θ = 44.1°) is clearly separated and stronger than in 0Cr and 3Cr; austenite lattice constant of 6Cr is 3.56 Å.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scan rate of 4° per min; 2θ range ~30–100°
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and determine austenite lattice parameter

characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite uniformly distributed in austenite matrix; 6Cr shows predominantly angular/block-like ferrite particles, more numerous and coarser than in 3Cr.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-2100F, operated at a voltage of 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite of 6Cr shows heavy dislocation content; κ-carbide superlattice is very weak in austenite SADP (indexed [001]γ) and κ-carbide sizes too small to identify. In the ferrite a DO3 superlattice is observed and nano-scale DO3 phases clearly appear in DF images of the 6Cr strip.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: bright-field and dark-field imaging; 500 nm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine dislocations and carbide/ordered phases in austenite and ferrite
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured composition of the 6Cr strip: Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8 wt.%.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine actual chemical composition of strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SJ-600G Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 6Cr strip is 6.46 g/cm³.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average density of the strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MTS Criterion Model 44 mechanical property tester, 10 kN capacity
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 6Cr: YS 652±5 MPa, UTS 953±9 MPa, TE 31.6±1 %.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm; strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1; values averaged over 3 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Increase of δ-ferrite fraction in Cr-containing strips can block dislocation propagation due to more phase-interface areas, which may decrease the plasticity.

interfaces.interface_notes: In the as-cast 0Cr strip κ-carbides are visible only at the austenite/ferrite phase boundary (DF image), i.e. phase boundaries are preferred precipitation sites; for 6Cr the austenite/ferrite interfaces add barriers to dislocation glide.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Solidification follows the FA (ferrite-to-austenite) mode: L (liquid) → L+δ (high-temperature ferrite) → L+δ+γ (austenite) → δ+γ. δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt during near-rapid solidification.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Slip bands are observed in austenite of the strips during deformation; average spacing between slip bands ~80 nm in as-cast 6Cr (vs ~90 nm in as-cast 0Cr), and average widths of slip bands in as-cast 6Cr are 12.5 nm. Narrow slip-band spacing suggests higher strain-hardening rate.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: As-cast 6Cr compared with as-cast Cr-free (0Cr): yield strength 652±5 MPa is lower than 0Cr (724±16 MPa); ultimate tensile strength 953±9 MPa is higher than 0Cr (924±24 MPa); total elongation 31.6±1 % is lower than 0Cr (40.8±8 %); steady-stage strain hardening rate (2266 MPa) is higher than 0Cr (1626 MPa). Cr addition increases strength and strain-hardening rate while reducing total elongation of as-cast strips.

processing_steps.method: induction melting of high purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.9%), Al (99.9%), C (99.8%) and Cr (99.9%)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot was made from high purity elements and reheated to melt by an induction coil before casting.

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting: liquid metal poured into a copper mold
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Mold rotating speed 600 r/min; obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm; this as-cast state received no post-solidification heat treatment.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests on a MTS Criterion Model 44 tester with 10 kN capacity; each test supported by more than three tensile specimens; values shown are averaged over 3 measurements (as-cast condition).
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge size of 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm

strain_hardening_rate.note: average strain hardening rate in the steady hardening stage

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of as-cast 6Cr rises to a high stress level (close to the 1000 MPa gridline) and terminates near 22–26% strain, with a small load drop before final fracture.

defects.dislocation_density: high (heavy dislocation content; more dislocations than 0Cr; slightly higher than 9Cr)

precipitates.distribution: in austenite matrix (superlattice very weak in SADP)

defects.dislocation_density: only a few dislocations occasionally observed in the ferrite

phases_present.morphology: predominantly angular/block-like particles, more numerous and coarser than 3Cr

precipitates.distribution: clearly appear in ferrite of 6Cr strip (DF images)
precipitates.type: DO3 phase (nano-scale ordered domains in ferrite)

microstructure_list.region: ferrite particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) microstructure with austenite as the major matrix phase; δ-ferrite uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix. For the 6Cr strip the ferrite fraction is 14.8 vol% and the δ(110) reflection is clearly stronger than in 0Cr and 3Cr, indicating Cr promotes ferrite; ferrite particles are predominantly angular/block-like.

unmapped_findings: Measured (ICP) composition of the as-cast 6Cr strip: Fe Bal., Mn 29.1, Al 9.9, C 1.2, Cr 6.8 wt.% (Table 1).
Nominal/series composition of the studied alloy system is Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr (x = 0, 3, 6, 9) wt.%.
As-cast 6Cr strip constituent phases by XRD: austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ), austenite as major matrix phase; austenite lattice constant 3.56 Å; δ(110) reflection at 2θ = 44.1°.
Ferrite fraction of as-cast 6Cr strip measured by Gatan Digital Micrograph: 14.8 vol%; Cr addition changes ferrite shape from rod-like to block-like (6Cr is block-like).
Only a few dislocations are occasionally observed in the ferrite of all strips; the as-cast 6Cr austenite has heavy dislocation content (slightly higher than 9Cr).
In the as-cast 6Cr and 9Cr strips a DO3 superlattice belonging to an ordered ferrite phase is observed, and nano-scale DO3 phases clearly appear in ferrite dark-field images.

Cr addition suppressed the precipitation of nano-scale κ-carbides in the austenite of as-cast strips; the κ-carbide superlattice in the 6Cr austenite SADP is very weak and κ-carbide sizes are too small to identify.
As-cast 6Cr strip produced under near-rapid solidification: strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm; no post-solidification heat treatment.

For the as-cast 6Cr strip after tensile fracture, average spacing between slip bands is ~80 nm and average width of slip bands is 12.5 nm; finer slip bands with smaller spacing normally accompany higher ductility, but as-cast 6Cr has the lowest elongation due to its high initial dislocation density.
